title: The Terms of Exchange
text: At that, Father turned his gaze toward the mongrel lizardman.
“…They wanted to go themselves. They demanded to participate in the wave and become a force for good. No one’s forcing them.”
Well, as expected, Itsuki, convinced of his own righteousness, didn’t seem inclined to listen at all.
“I understand perfectly well that you’re controlling them with slave crests so they die if they don’t say things like that. Don’t worry. I’ll save you all.”
“Uhh—”
The rabbit man looked like he couldn’t hold back from butting in any longer. Well then, I supposed I’d have to lend a hand here, I say.
“Silence Lance V.”
One little prick, and the noisy one goes quiet—a silencing skill, indeed.
“Wha—!? What are you—”
Couldn’t be helped. I shut him up.
“Itsuki, this is another world. When in Rome, do as the Romans do. The existence of slavery here can’t be helped.”
“It absolutely can be helped! Naofumi! You’re wrong! And with what you did to her again, I’m now certain of it!”

“That crazy woman over there is none of my business. But as for slavery, yeah, I’m in the wrong there. I won’t deny it. In normal Japan, your words would be perfectly correct. But this country runs on it. Same goes for the demi-human nations—they keep human slaves too. Just who do you think you are?”

The rabbit man, looking like he absolutely had to jump in, tried to step forward, so I grabbed him by the scruff of the neck, I say. His hands and feet were already poofing into rabbit form. Way too excited. Father was signaling the rabbit man with his hand to calm down. He seemed worried the transformation might trigger a worse seizure if it went too far. Bit of a hassle—should I just put him to sleep for now?
“What do you mean, ‘who do I think I am’!”

“Exactly what it sounds like. You know the saying? Humans are at their most cruel when they’re absolutely convinced they’re righteous. After all, if you’re certain you’re right, anything is permissible. That kind of conviction can turn a person endlessly brutal.”

Oooh… Father’s words struck deep into me, I say. Indeed, back then, convinced of my own righteousness, I had condemned Father. Well… you always act convinced you’re in the right too, you know… I could almost hear imaginary Father saying in my head, but I am a sinner, I say. I act in loyalty to the justice defined by Filo-tan and Father, so there’s no mistake there. No, wait, isn’t that exactly the root of the cruelty…? said imaginary Big Sister in my head, but no, that’s wrong. Father and the others are absolute justice—doubting them is simply not allowed.
“Hmph… quite the smooth talker, aren’t you? Isn’t it your rhetoric he’s been mimicking, which is why he’s become so combative? You’ve given him a terrible education!”
“Who knows.”
Itsuki and Father glared daggers at each other, trading barbs back and forth. Father, what exactly are you aiming for here?
“I have heard everything Lord Itsuki had to say!”

And here came Trash. Impressive timing, honestly. A senile old menace who’d perfected the art of picking fights out of thin air. How should I carve him up this loop, I wondered. Honestly, since Fleon-chan seemed to have taken a liking to Trash, I was starting to think I should go easy on making him suffer through hell. Apparently, it was Trash who came up with the plan to destroy the Filolial-sama eggs, but there was also word that he’d given orders not to actually carry it out… It was Takt who did it, an outrage carried out without Trash’s permission. I’d have to keep Trash on standby as a backup playmate for Fleon-chan in case Itsuki wouldn’t play with her.

This time around, I was honestly getting sick of Itsuki and wanted to mess with him a little. I needed to come up with a plan to cook up the Crimson Swine while also getting Trash to be Fleon-chan’s playmate. In the previous loop, Fleon-chan had seemed a bit lonely since Itsuki hadn’t played with her much. This time, with Trash around, if brainwashing Itsuki wasn’t on the table, I wanted Trash to play with her instead. Filolial Cross, was it? Either way, bravo, Trash, for pulling off the exact farce you’d planned from the very start!
By the way, this loop’s Father was muttering a small “Alright…” under his breath. Guess he figured picking a fight with Itsuki had bought him some time.
“Then how about this? The Heroes fight each other, and whoever wins, their claim is deemed correct.”
“Heh…”

Father wore a bold, confident smile, as if he’d been waiting for exactly this. Seeing that attitude, both the Crimson Swine and Trash furrowed their brows. They probably thought it was a bluff. I knew exactly what Father’s plan was, I say. Using the Shield’s counterattack effect to slowly poison and weaken Itsuki, then claim victory. When I first saw that plan, I trembled with admiration, I say. Doing whatever it takes to win—truly a valiant sight, so very like Father.
“For a Hero to be using a slave… I’d only heard rumors of it, but if Lord Itsuki objects, then I shall command it myself. A duel it is!”
The mongrel lizardman and the rabbit man both clenched their fists in unison, glaring daggers at Trash like he was garbage.
“If Lord Itsuki wins, all the Shield Hero’s slaves shall be freed. If the Shield Hero wins, the matter shall be dropped.”
“…I don’t think that makes any sense?”
“What doesn’t make sense about it?! It’s a chance to prove justice!”
The flow of events closely resembled the loop where I’d stayed in Melromarc, but this time, Father wore a bold, predatory expression, like a hunter watching prey step right into his trap.
“That’s Itsuki’s logic. What’s in it for me?”
“There’s plenty in it for you, isn’t there? The right to use slaves however you please.”
“Think carefully about what it means to be granted, like some kind of reward, a right you already had from the start. And besides, the slaves I’m using are on loan.”

The flow matched the loop where I’d stayed in Melromarc… but I could sense Father’s confident demeanor steering things toward a different outcome this time. What was he planning, I wondered? Father glanced my way, as if to say it’s fine.
“Well, if you want a duel that badly, I’ll take you up on it.”

Father beckoned Itsuki forward with a “come at me” gesture, taunting him. The soldiers were surrounding the mongrel lizardman and rabbit man to restrain the slaves. The lizardman and rabbit man glared back, ready to counterattack the instant anyone lunged at them. Meanwhile, Yuki-chan and the other Filolial-sama were intimidating the soldiers and scattering them off.
“You’ve taken the bait! Very well! Let’s settle this!”
“However!”
In a loud, ringing voice, Father pointed at Trash and the Crimson Swine, and laughed.
“If I win, Eclair Seaetto, currently imprisoned in this country’s dungeon, is to be released and placed under my command.”
“Gah—!”
“Bwehehheeyyy!”
Trash faltered, and the Crimson Swine burst into tears and screams instantly. Given such an unfavorable proposal, they couldn’t exactly keep their mouths shut.
“Do you honestly think such a condition would be accepted!? Fool!”
“Bwoohaaa! Oink oink!”
“Just who exactly is this person…?”
Itsuki looked back and forth between Trash and the Crimson Swine with a “huh?” expression. Like, who is that supposed to be?
“She’s a serious criminal! It shall not be allowed!”

“Well now, isn’t this something. Lord Bow Hero here is about to duel in order to free demi-human slaves, and yet the knight who fought to protect demi-humans from soldiers conducting slave hunts in the disaster zone during this country’s very first wave—that knight is somehow the serious criminal?”
“…What do you mean by that?”

Itsuki tilted his head and glanced over, and the mongrel lizardman simply nodded in confirmation. Sure, if the duel opponent were me or Ren, they might’ve been able to smooth it over, but to someone as strongly principled as Itsuki, Éclair’s actions would surely look like the right thing to do. Give him the information that someone who did the right thing was being treated as a serious criminal, and even someone other than Itsuki would end up making that exact face.
